phil-log-01-c2.text: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Validity and Soundness. Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-log-01-c2.quote: it takes a form that makes it impossible for the premises to be true and the conclusion nevertheless to be false
phil-log-01-c2.claim: An argument is valid if the conclusion must be true whenever the premises are true.

phil-log-01-c2.text: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Validity and Soundness. Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-log-01-c2.quote: it is both valid, and all of its premises are actually true
phil-log-01-c2.claim: An argument is sound if it is valid and all its premises are actually true.

phil-log-01-c3.text: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (2025). Inductive Logic. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-log-01-c3.quote: In a deductive logic the truth of the premises of a good argument guarantees the truth of its conclusion.
phil-log-01-c3.claim: Deductive arguments aim for certainty. If the premises are true, the conclusion must be true.
